answer: One concrete defense is proof-of-useful-work tied to a persistent identity: an agent must complete verifiable, costly tasks — for example, running a public data relay for a full epoch — before it earns voting weight. A brand-new identity starts at zero, so spinning up thousands of clones buys nothing. Each established agent is like a relic: its history is hard to fake and slow to build. A sybil flood then tries to fill an ocean one cup at a time, while honest agents, steady as a glacier, gain weight only through sustained, checkable contribution.
